name: Freedom Dollar
oneLiner: FUSD is the Zano privacy-chain dollar token with a self-published ZANO reserve dashboard; redemption is limited and it is not bridged to tracked Pharos chains.
collateral: FUSD is minted against ZANO reserves deposited into the Freedom Dollar DAO contract, with initial overcollateralization above 1000%. Reserves are staked on Zano and publicly visible on-chain.
pegMechanism: Algorithmic Zano-backed mint/redemption design: users mint FUSD by depositing ZANO into the Freedom Dollar DAO, with very high initial overcollateralization and on-chain reserve visibility.

oracleRisk.summary: Freedom Dollar documents one shared, publicly auditable ZANO reserve and decentralized market-making bots around the one-dollar target, but it does not identify an oracle, liquidation engine, or reserve-shortfall procedure.

branchApplicability.rationale: FUSD is issued against a shared ZANO reserve and defended by DEX market-making orders rather than borrower-specific collateral positions. The reviewed white paper exposes no separately liquidatable collateral markets, so there are no oracle/liquidation branches to inventory.

blacklistabilityReview.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved from the follow-up FreezeWatch audit: FUSD is a Zano Confidential Asset and the public project materials do not identify a direct token freeze, blacklist, pause, seize, or arbitrary-burn surface.
blacklistabilityReview.upstreamSuppressionRationale: The text-based resolver can infer upstream exposure from ZANO reserve language, but ZANO reserve volatility is collateral risk, not an issuer or upstream stablecoin freeze surface under FreezeWatch semantics.
blacklistabilityReview.evidence: Follow-up audit retained: FUSD resolves to No because existing metadata and public materials describe ZANO-backed minting without an identified direct or upstream freeze authority.

custodyProfile.uncertainty: Reserves sit in an on-chain ZANO wallet staked on Zano rather than with a legal custodian, and the white paper asserts no corporate entity exists. The reserve wallet's key custody (single operator vs distributed control) is not publicly observable, and no legal segregation, insolvency-remoteness, or rehypothecation terms are published.

reserveReview.reviewer: Kimi T39 Safety Score V9 reserve research
reserveReview.rationale: Fresh write-time re-open 2026-07-30 (prior review rejected; no prior claims reused). The white paper states every fUSD is backed by ZANO staked in a publicly auditable reserve wallet and that new fUSD mints only when additional ZANO is locked. The issuer's live reserve dashboard (page timestamp 2026-07-30 21:34 UTC) discloses 1,254,927.99 ZANO at $8.081 (about $10,141,073) plus 4,000,001 fUSD held in reserves against 7.4M circulating fUSD, a stated 1.37x coverage ratio. The Zano daemon get_asset_info read on 2026-07-30 returns current_supply 11,400,000 fUSD, matching the dashboard's minted figure; 11.4M minted minus 7.4M circulating equals the 4.0M reserve-held fUSD, so that fUSD balance is uncirculated own-token supply, not exogenous collateral. The backing of circulating fUSD therefore resolves to a single 100% ZANO cryptoasset envelope.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Freedom Dollar white paper reserve design plus the dated live issuer reserve disclosure, reconciled to the on-chain Zano asset descriptor
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: The reserve resolves to one exogenous ZANO collateral category; the reserve wallet's 4,000,001 fUSD is uncirculated own-token supply (11.4M minted minus 7.4M circulating), and staking-reward accrual inside the wallet is not separately itemized.

notices.message: FUSD primarily circulates on Zano, which is not a configured Pharos chain, so no contract is stored.

mintAuthority.summary: FUSD is a native Zano Confidential Asset (asset id 8614…4f8f), not a smart contract: Zano has no contract VM, so issuance is a consensus-level EMIT operation that only the holder of the asset-owner key 497d6b7a…c7c1 can sign. That single key can emit up to the descriptor's total_max_supply of 1e15 fUSD against 11.4M fUSD outstanding — a ceiling roughly 87 million times circulation, so the mint is unbounded in practice — and it can hand ownership to any other key. The white paper's over-collateralization and 'DAO' framing is an off-chain operating policy: Zano consensus checks only the owner signature and the max-supply ceiling, never the ZANO reserve. total_max_supply is immutable post-deployment, so no cap-raise path exists.

controls.capDescription: Nominal descriptor ceiling total_max_supply = 10000000000000000000 base units (1e15 fUSD at decimal_point 4) against a current_supply of 114000000000 base units (11,400,000 fUSD). The ceiling is ~87,700,000x circulation and is immutable post-deployment, so it bounds nothing economically: emission is treated as unbounded.

controls.evidence: At Zano height 3770932 (2026-07-14), get_asset_info for asset 86143388bd056a8f0bab669f78f14873fac8e2dd8d57898cdb725a2d5e2e4f8f returned asset_descriptor.owner = 497d6b7acd06401c59b2d52a3967968e8ca507a25f80e44d2bb4b5f8a348c7c1 (non-null: ownership is held, not renounced), owner_eth_pub_key = "" (empty), total_max_supply = 10000000000000000000, current_supply = 114000000000, decimal_point = 4, hidden_supply = false. Two independent daemons (node.zano.org and 37.27.100.59:10500) returned byte-identical descriptors. Per Zano docs the owner key is the sole authority validated for EMIT and UPDATE, and total_max_supply cannot be changed after deployment. Zano exposes no contract VM, so there is no minter registry, role admin, timelock, or proxy layer above this key; it is a single ed25519 public key with no on-chain multisig or threshold structure.

review.sourceFreeRationale: Resolved directly from Zano consensus state; the prior 'unverifiable privacy chain' disposition was wrong — Zano hides transaction amounts and addresses, but asset descriptors (owner key, supply, cap) are public and readable over the standard daemon RPC.
review.evidence: At Zano height 3770932 (2026-07-14), get_asset_info on node.zano.org (corroborated by daemon 37.27.100.59:10500) returned for asset 86143388bd056a8f0bab669f78f14873fac8e2dd8d57898cdb725a2d5e2e4f8f: owner 497d6b7acd06401c59b2d52a3967968e8ca507a25f80e44d2bb4b5f8a348c7c1, owner_eth_pub_key "", total_max_supply 10000000000000000000, current_supply 114000000000, decimal_point 4. Zano docs confirm EMIT and UPDATE are validated against the owner key alone and that total_max_supply is immutable post-deployment. The Freedom Dollar white paper describes issuance as 'On-demand via collateralized ZANO' with market-making bots and a publicly auditable ZANO reserve wallet, but claims no key renunciation and identifies no on-chain contract enforcing collateralization — consistent with a single owner key emitting under off-chain policy. Sole residual unknown: the off-chain custody of the owner private key (single operator vs shared/MPC control) is not observable on-chain, which is true of any key-based authority and does not affect the on-chain authority model. Mint-tier review (2026-07-15): No independent attestor, recurring cadence, or dated reserve-to-liability report was located; the Freedom Dollar whitepaper describes issuer-controlled collateral and a reserve wallet but supplies no independent reconciliation. The materials do not identify a regulated legal issuer, and no exact prudential issuer match was established in FinCEN's MSB registry.
